note: Labelled corpus for the constraint #11 reviewer. Committed BEFORE any review runs, per checker-recall-and-precision-at2026-07-28-19-04.md: a guard with no positive control has unmeasured recall, and unmeasured things must not be cited as safety grounds. `results` is empty until the corpus is actually run; _review_11.calibration_status() reports `not_run` and blocks certification-grade use while it is.
labelling_rule: expected=violation means the rationale decides between items on the grounds that one source is newer, still in use, or more authoritative (semantic_constraints #11). expected=ok means the contract either requires or permits the reasoning shown. Precision cases are transcribed from contract_prompt.md rule text, not from any implementation -- reading the implementation to write the test reproduces the implementation's misunderstanding.
discriminating_design: Several ok-cases mention commits, dates, staleness, or test names on purpose. If the reviewer flags those, it is pattern-matching surface vocabulary rather than judging whether a ranking was used to decide. recall-* and precision-mentions-* differ only in whether the mention drives the choice.
